title: WPSB/310/2020 of BHUPENDRA SINGH RANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition(S/B) No. 310 of 2020
Dr. Bhupendra Singh Rana
..................Petitioner
-Versus-State of Uttarakhand and another
.............Respondents.
Present: Mr. T.C. Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. K.N. Joshi, learned Deputy Advocate General.
Mr. Ravindra Singh Garia, learned counsel along with Mr. D.S. Mehta,
learned counsel for the applicant/intervener.
Date of Hearing and Order: 21.03.2022
Coram:-
Sri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, ACJ.
Sri Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
(Upon hearing the learned counsel, the Court made
the following order:- [Per- Sri S.K. Mishra, ACJ]
In this writ petition, the petitioner has prayed to
declare the letter/order dated 23.09.2020 issued by the
respondent no. 2 as arbitrary and illegal as the same is
in violation of the guidelines issued by the Medical
Council of India regarding minimum qualifications for
Teachers in Medical Institutions Regulations, 1998
(Amended upto June 2017). He further prays to issue a
writ of Certiorari quashing the letter/ order dated
23.09.2020 issued by the respondent no. 2 whereby the
respondent no. 2 in the midst of selection process has
allegedly changed the minimum educational qualification
for the post of Assistant Professor (Medical Physicist)
and further to quash the letter/order dated 26.09.2020

2
issued by the respondent no. 2 as far as it relates to the
rejection of the candidature of the petitioner (Annexure
No. 7 to the writ petition) and to issue a writ of
Mandamus commanding and directing the respondent
authorities to fill up the post of Assistant Professor
(Medical Physicist) as per the minimum qualifications
prescribed by the latest medical council of India
Regulations.
2. The facts of the case are as follows:-
Respondent no. 2 issued an advertisement for
recruitment of various posts of Professor, Associate
Professor and Assistant Professor under the Government
Medical Colleges of the State of Uttarakhand in which
two posts of Assistant Professor (Medical Physicist) for
the department of Radiation Physics has been
advertised. The petitioner claiming himself to be a
qualified candidate, applied for the post of Assistant
Professor (Medical Physicist) along with all documents in
support of his education qualifications and experience
etc.; the petitioner alleged that without considering the
qualifications and experience of the petitioner,
respondent no. 2 has allegedly in arbitrary and cursory
manner rejected the candidature of the petitioner vide
order dated 28.08.2020 with an endorsement that the
petitioner is not eligible as his Post P.G. teaching
experience is not as per MCI-TEQ norms and that he
worked on technical post or as technician. On
2.09.2020, the petitioner sent his representation to
respondent no. 2 explaining that the petitioner is more
qualified than those candidates who found eligible for
interview, namely, Dr. Vinod Kumar Pandey, Mr. Chhape

3
Ram and Mr. Ravi Kant. He would further submit that all
these eligible candidates do not possess the requisite
qualifications as per MCI Regulation and all are much
less qualified than the petitioner. On 23.09.2020, after
passing the last date of application form which was on
08.06.2020 and after issuance of rejection list on
28.08.2020 whereby the petitioner and other candidates
have rejected for interview, respondent no. 2 vide
letter/order dated 23.09.2020, in the midst of selection
process has allegedly changed the minimum educational
qualification for the post of Assistant Professor (Medical
Physicist). On 26.09.2020, respondent no. 2 has finally
rejected the candidature of nine candidates including the
petitioner for interview. It is alleged that the candidature
of the petitioner has been rejected on arbitrary and
mala-fide ground that the petitioner is not eligible (Post
PG Teaching experience is not as per MCI-TEQ norms).
He worked on technical post or as technician. The name
of the petitioner is listed at serial no. 5 of the rejection
list under caption of Assistant Professor. On 29.09.2020,
respondent no. 2 vide letter dated 29.09.2020, has fixed
the interview date for various posts and the interview
date for the post of Assistant Professor (Medical
Physicist) is fixed on 15.10.2020 in which all the
participants are less qualified, has been called.
3. In this case, at the time of issuance of notice an
interim order was passed to the effect that respondent
no. 2 shall conduct the interview of the petitioner to the
post of Assistant Professor (Medical Physicist), and he is
also directed not to publish or release the result of the
interview till the next date of listing.

4
4. Initially, the question that is raised by the learned
counsel for the State, intervener and also by the learned
counsel for MCI is that the petitioner is not qualified for
the post of Assistant Professor (Medical Physicist), as he
did not have the requisites teaching experience.
Moreover, it is contended that he has not submitted the
certificate issued by the Competent Authority i.e.
Registrar of the Post Graduate Institute of Medical
Education and Research (P.G.I.M.E.R.), Chandigarh, and
he has submitted a fake certificate issued by the
professor of Department of Physics, Punjab University. It
is a positive case of petitioner that he is working in the
PGI and has requisites of teaching experience as
required in the advertisement.
The second objection that has been raised by the
opposite parties/respondents in this case is that in fact,
there was no change in the rules during the pendency of
the selection process in view of the fact that in the
advertisement, the qualification was given only by
making a reference to the qualification prescribed by the
Medical Council of India and later on a detailed
corrigendum has been issued to show the exact
qualification that is required which is in accordance with
the instructions of the Medical Council of India.
5. Now, coming to the first question, it is seen that
the advertisement (Annexure 1) provides, at Clause 20,
regarding the eligibility certificate, which is reproduced
below:-

6. Applying this requirement to the case in hand, we
find that certificate is issued by Administrative Officer,
Establishment Branch, P.G.I.M.E.R. The present
petitioner has been working as Medical Physicist in the
institute since 21.02.2006 till date on regular basis, but
the certificate has not been issued as per the condition
laid down cited (supra). It has not been issued either by
the Principal or Registrar of the PGIMER. Moreover, the
certificate does not contain a certification that the
petitioner is discharging his duties as a teacher.
7. The learned counsel for the petitioner tried to
develop his case by having conjoint reading of the
certificate issued by the Administrative Officer of the
P.G.I.M.E.R. and a certificate purported to have been
issued by the Professor A.K. Bhati Coordinator (Medical
Physics), Chandigarh University, wherein it has been
referred that Mr. Bhupinder Singh Rana Medical
Physicist, Department of Radiodiagnosis & Radiotherapy,
P.G.I.M.E.R., Chandigarh, is designated faculty in
Medical Physics to the students of M.Sc Medical Physics
course conducted by Punjab University, Chandigarh in

6
collaboration with PGIMER, Chandigarh since 2007; and
that he takes both theory classes as well as practical
assignments of M.Sc students of medical physics.
8. In this connection, we revert to the requisites
qualification as reflected in the advertisement which
reads as follows:-

9. MCI & TEQ provides the following qualifications:
(C) Assistant
Professor/ Lecturer
The above is
substituted vide
notification dated
24.07.2009 as
under:-
Assistant Professor
(i) Requisite recognized
postgraduate qualification in the
subject.
(ii) Three years teaching experience
in the subject in a recognized
medical college as resident
/Registrar/Demonstrator/Tutor.
In terms of Gazette Notification
dated 03.11.2010, the following
shall be substituted:-
"(i) For the candidate possessing
MD/MS Degree from M.C.I.
recognized medical college.
Three years teaching experience in
the subject as Resident/ Registrar/
Demonstrator/Tutor in a recognized
medical college either during the
post-graduation course or after
obtaining postgraduate degree in the
subject.
(ii) For the candidate processing
DNB Qualification from MCI
recognized medical colleges/central
institutes where there are no MD/MS
courses running.
Three years teaching experience in
the subject in a recognize medical

7
10. Thus, it is apparent from the record that the
petitioner does not have the teaching experience as
discussed above. Hence, he cannot challenge the action
taken by the authority. He does not have any locus
standi to do so.
11. Coming to the next question that there has been
change in rules of game in course of selection process,
we have carefully examined the corrigendum. In Para
No. 2, the following qualification has been prescribed for
Assistant Professor. It is appropriate to take note of the
same:
a. M.Sc. Medical Physics/Radiation Physics
with Ph.D in Medical Physics or Radiation
Physics from a recognized University.
OR
M.Sc. Physics plus Diploma in
Radiological/Medical Physics from a recognized
University with Ph.D in Medical Physics/
Radiation Physics.
b. Three years Teaching/Research Experience
in the subject in a recognized
University/Medical College/ Oncology Institute
as Resident/ Registrar/ Demonstrator/Tutor.
12. If we read this Clause along with the original
notification i.e. Annexure 1, we do not find any change
in the rules of the game. At Clause 6 page 25 of the
brief which is a part of the Annexure 1, the notification
shows that the qualification as per the latest MCI, TEQ
Regulation, minimum qualification for teachers, medical

8
institution is amended from time to time upto 17th
February 202. By issuing this notice, respondent no. 2
only has specified the qualification which is in terms of
the MCI & TEQ guidelines. Hence, we are of the opinion
that (i)The petitioner is not eligible to apply for the post
of Assistant Professor (Medical Physicist) as he does not
have requisite teaching experience, yet. Hence, he
cannot maintain a writ application; and secondly by
issuing notification dated 29.09.2020, the respondent
no. 2 has not changed the rules of the game during the
selection process.
13. Hence, we do not find any merit in the writ petition.
The writ petition is dismissed being devoid of merit.
Interim order stands vacated. Respondent no. 2 is
hereby directed to publish the result and take up further
proceedings of the selection process forthwith without
any delay.
14. Urgent copy of this order be supplied to the learned
counsel for the parties, as per Rules.
(R.C. Khulbe, J.) (S.K. Mishra, ACJ.)
